2_Introduction: The device displayed a champion PCE of 24.6984%, with a VOC of 1.1814 V, a JSC of 26.32 mA/cm², and an FF of 79.4301%. The perovskite ink, prepared from Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 at 1.65 mol/L, formed the base layer for subsequent fabrication steps. The precursor solution was spin-coated on the substrate at 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s. During the second step, 150 µL of CB as anti-solvent was quickly dripped onto the centre of the perovskite film 15 s before the end of the spin-coating process. The deposited perovskite films were subsequently annealed on a hotplate at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite layer—engineered with a carefully balanced A-site cation mixture—exhibits enhanced phase stability and suppressed halide segregation due to the synergistic steric and electronic contributions of formamidinium (FA⁺) as the dominant cation, methylammonium (MA⁺) for lattice tightening, and cesium (Cs⁺) for tolerance factor optimization (~0.98), collectively mitigating octahedral tilting and reducing non-radiative recombination pathways; the 1.65 mol/L precursor concentration, combined with the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/5 s for wet-film formation followed by 5500 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent extraction), enables controlled nucleation density and kinetic suppression of premature crystallization, while the precisely timed (15 s before spin cessation) and volumetrically calibrated (150 µL) chlorobenzene antisolvent quenching induces instantaneous supersaturation, promoting uniform nucleation across the substrate and suppressing pinhole formation—evidenced by high-coverage, low-defect-density optical micrographs and homogeneous photoluminescence (PL) mapping with strong intensity and long-lived monoexponential decay (τ₁ ≈ 320 ns), indicating minimal trap-assisted recombination and efficient radiative recombination; XRD analysis further confirms phase purity through the absence of residual PbI₂ (no peak at ~12.6°) and suppression of δ-phase impurities, with narrow (110) peak FWHM (<0.12°) and negligible lattice strain, reflecting highly ordered, low-defect, large-grained crystallites grown during the 110 °C/15 min thermal annealing that simultaneously drives volatile byproduct removal and grain boundary healing—collectively yielding optimized interfacial energetics, reduced interfacial recombination velocity, and balanced charge extraction, culminating in a VOC of 1.1814 V, a JSC of 26.32 mA/cm², an FF of 79.4301%, and a champion PCE of 24.6984%.
